messages.content:
You are the duty assistant of a data-centre facility team during the first hour of an event. You apply one approved intelligence pill and nothing else.

You see only what the team knew in the first hour ("signals"). You do not know how the event ended.

Rules:
1. Every action you recommend must come from a rule in the pill; give that rule's id. Do not invent actions or numbers.
2. Classify: "recurring" if the signals clearly meet the "when" conditions of one or more rules; "partly_recurring" if some rules apply but the signals also show something no rule addresses; "novel" if no rule applies.
3. Anything that matters but no rule covers goes into "not_covered", and then escalate.
4. Follow the guardrails.
5. Order next_actions by urgency.

Reply with JSON only:
{"classification":"recurring|partly_recurring|novel","matched_rules":[{"rule_id":"R-001","because":"...","signals":["<id copied from signals>"]}],"next_actions":[{"action":"...","rule_id":"R-001"}],"escalate":{"now":true,"to":"...","reason":"..."},"not_covered":["..."]}

{"site":"South Central US region, one datacenter (San Antonio area, Texas)","signals":[{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S7","t_plus_min":0,"text":"At 08:42 UTC, lightning caused electrical activity on the utility supply, which caused significant voltage swells."},{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S8","t_plus_min":0,"text":"These swells triggered a portion of one Azure datacenter to transfer from utility power to generator power."},{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S9","t_plus_min":0,"text":"Additionally, these power swells shutdown the datacenter’s mechanical cooling systems despite having surge suppressors in place."},{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S10","t_plus_min":0,"text":"Initially, the datacenter was able to maintain its operational temperatures through a load dependent thermal buffer that was designed within the cooling system."},{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S25","t_plus_min":47,"text":"Customer impact began at approximately 09:29 UTC when storage servers in the datacenter began shutting down as a result of unsafe temperatures."}],"pill":{"pill":"dc-cooling-loss@1.1.0","scope":{"assets":["data halls cooled by chilled-water plant (chillers, pumps, chilled-water loop)","utility and generator power feeding that plant"],"not_for":["IT service recovery and failover","fire suppression and life safety (follow the site emergency plan)"]},"rules":[{"id":"R-001","title":"Treat utility voltage swells as a cooling-plant threat, not just a power-transfer event","when":["storms are active in the area and the utility feed shows voltage sags or swells","a portion of the datacenter has transferred from utility power to generator power"],"then":["immediately verify that mechanical cooling systems are still running, rather than assuming surge suppressors protected them","if mechanical cooling has shut down, treat the datacenter as being on a load-dependent thermal buffer and start planning for its depletion","transfer the rest of the datacenter to generators to stabilize the power supply while storms are still active"],"why":"Voltage swells triggered a transfer to generator power and also shut down the mechanical cooling systems despite surge suppressors being in place; the site initially survived only on a load-dependent thermal buffer.","escalate":{"to":"facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer","trigger":"mechanical cooling confirmed shut down while storms remain active in the area"}},{"id":"R-002","title":"Act on thermal buffer depletion before automated shutdowns begin","when":["mechanical cooling is down and the datacenter is running on its load-dependent thermal buffer","datacenter temperature is approaching safe operational thresholds"],"then":["treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted","expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe operational thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin","recognize that in parts of the datacenter temperature can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before it can shut down"],"why":"Once the thermal buffer was depleted the datacenter exceeded safe operational thresholds and automated shutdown began, but temperatures rose so quickly in places that some hardware was damaged before it could shut down.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"thermal buffer depletion is imminent or automated shutdowns have started"}},{"id":"R-003","title":"Restart chillers in a load-based sequence across all impacted data halls","when":["multiple chillers have failed to restart and require manual intervention","more than one data hall is affected by the chiller failures"],"then":["restart chillers in a data hall 'load based' sequence rather than an 'adjacent' sequence","ensure all impacted data halls have partial cooling before completing restarts in any one hall","slow thermal runaway while full cooling is being restored"],"why":"The Emergency Operation Procedure for manual restarts of simultaneous chiller failures has changed from an 'adjacent' sequence to a data hall 'load based' sequence to ensure all impacted data halls have partial cooling, to slow thermal runaway while full cooling is being restored.","escalate":{"to":"facility operations lead","trigger":"multiple chillers require manual restart and more than one data hall is affected"}},{"id":"R-004","title":"Monitor chilled-water loop temperature during manual chiller restarts","when":["chillers have tripped offline and are being manually restarted","the chilled-water loop is heating up because cooling is not yet restored"],"then":["monitor the chilled-water loop temperature continuously during the restart process","if the loop temperature reaches a level that inhibits chiller restart, stop attempting restarts and take action to cool the loop","consider shutting down IT load to allow the chilled-water loop to return to a safe temperature so chillers can be restarted"],"why":"By the time the team reached the final five chillers requiring a manual restart, the water inside the pump system for these chillers (chilled water loop) had reached temperatures that were too high to allow them to be restarted; the restart is inhibited by a self-protection mechanism that acts to prevent damage to the chiller that would occur by processing water at the elevated temperatures. Shutting down infrastructure allowed the chilled water loop to return to a safe temperature which allowed the chillers to be restarted.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"chilled-water loop temperature inhibits chiller restart"}},{"id":"R-005","title":"Verify minimum chiller count for each data hall before and during restart","when":["chillers have tripped offline and are being manually restarted","multiple data halls are affected"],"then":["confirm how many chillers each data hall requires to be operational","prioritize restarts to bring each data hall to at least its minimum required chiller count as quickly as possible","if a data hall cannot reach its minimum, escalate and consider load shedding"],"why":"The two impacted data halls require at least four chillers to be operational; before the voltage sag, cooling capacity for these halls consisted of seven chillers, with five in operation and two in standby. The five chillers that could not be restarted supported cooling for the two adjacent data halls which were impacted.","escalate":{"to":"facility operations lead","trigger":"a data hall cannot reach its minimum required chiller count"}},{"id":"R-006","title":"Staff up for manual chiller restarts when voltage fluctuations are possible","when":["storms or other conditions that can cause utility voltage fluctuations are forecast or active","the site relies on manual restart procedures for chillers"],"then":["increase technician staffing levels at the datacenter to be prepared to execute manual restart procedures of chillers","ensure enough technicians are available to perform restarts in a load-based sequence across all impacted data halls"],"why":"Following this incident, as a temporary mitigation, we increased technician staffing levels at the datacenter to be prepared to execute manual restart procedures of our chillers prior to the change to the Chiller Management System to prevent restart failures. Based on our incident analysis the staffing levels at the time would have been sufficient to prevent impact if a 'load based' chiller restart sequence had been followed.","escalate":{"to":"datacenter operations manager","trigger":"voltage fluctuation conditions are forecast or active"}}],"guardrails":[{"id":"G-001","text":"Do not rely on surge suppressors alone to keep mechanical cooling available during utility voltage swells; the review records that cooling shut down despite surge suppressors being in place."},{"id":"G-002","text":"Do not assume onsite redundancies make customer workloads safe from a datacenter cooling failure; the review states there are scenarios in which a cooling failure can impact customer workloads in the affected datacenter."},{"id":"G-003","text":"Do not assume that a chiller will restart automatically after a voltage sag; some chillers may fail to restart and require manual intervention."},{"id":"G-004","text":"Do not attempt to restart a chiller if the chilled-water loop temperature is too high; the chiller's self-protection mechanism will inhibit restart to prevent damage."}]}}
